name: DWP — Workplace pension participation and savings trends (2009 to 2025)

model.name: DWP estimates derived from ONS ASHE
model.method: Participation is the share of employees ELIGIBLE for automatic enrolment who are saving into a workplace pension, estimated from the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (an employer survey of jobs), Great Britain, April reference period.
model.method_basis: DWP background information and methodology note accompanying the release

denominator_note: ELIGIBILITY IS PART OF THE IDENTITY. The denominator is employees eligible for automatic enrolment, defined by an earnings trigger and an age range that have both moved over the series. A participation rate whose denominator is unstated is uninterpretable, so it is carried on every claim rather than left in a methodology note.
period: ASHE April reference years 2009 to 2025, carried as calendar years
geographies: Great Britain — ASHE excludes Northern Ireland, so rows carry GB and not UK
coverage_note: What is READ: block 1 of sheets 1.3a (earnings band), 1.4 (age band) and 1.9a (region), each split Public / Private / Overall. What is deliberately NOT read and tallied by the build: the five unlabelled side-by-side blocks on each of those sheets, because every sheet holds six tables next to each other and only the first carries a descriptor — a number whose meaning is inferred from its column position is not a claim; and the other 21 data sheets, each of which is its own population decision.
diagnosis_upstream: Built on ASHE, an employer survey of jobs, where the certified policyengine-uk world is FRS-based, a household survey. A PE-vs-DWP participation gap is a survey-population difference before it is an engine question — the same axis the Low Pay Commission lane (#88) carries — and it must be sized before any engine defect is named, and then only through the citable-known-issue gate. Note also that PE-UK models pension CONTRIBUTIONS and their relief but has no representation of the pension commencement lump sum (verified at the certified pin, #98), so the pensions question this scorecard can ask is narrower than the pensions system.
